overview: Two of the four Gell and Coombs hypersensitivity types, distinguished by speed of onset and whether antibodies or T cells drive the reaction.
genZNote: Type I: instant regret (allergies). Type IV: the delayed callback (poison ivy, TB skin test).

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: An immediate, IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction triggered by mast cell and basophil degranulation.
aspects.valueB: A delayed, T-cell-mediated hypersensitivity reaction not involving antibodies.

aspects.label: Primary Mediator
aspects.valueA: IgE antibodies bound to mast cells/basophils, with histamine release upon antigen cross-linking.
aspects.valueB: Sensitized T cells (Th1) releasing cytokines that recruit and activate macrophages.

aspects.label: Time Course
aspects.valueA: Immediate — occurs within minutes of antigen exposure.
aspects.valueB: Delayed — typically develops 24-72 hours after antigen exposure.

aspects.label: Classic Examples
aspects.valueA: Anaphylaxis, allergic rhinitis, asthma, food allergies, urticaria.
aspects.valueB: Contact dermatitis (e.g. poison ivy), tuberculin skin test (PPD) reaction, graft rejection.
